blocks.text: Degenerative disorders are conditions with progressive deterioration of nerve cells in the brain, spinal cord or peripheral nerves.

items: Parkinson's disease: progressive death or weakening of the dopamine-producing neurons of the brain, leading to movement problems and changes in thinking.
Huntington's disease: progressive damage to neurons in the brain, leading to movement disorders, decline in thinking and psychiatric symptoms.
Multiple sclerosis: an autoimmune disease of the CNS that damages the myelin sheath, leading to loss of vision, pain, fatigue and poor coordination.

blocks.caption: Alzheimer's disease
rows: a progressive degenerative brain disorder affecting memory, thinking and behaviour; it leads to dementia in older adults
a combination of genetic, environmental and lifestyle factors
begin with mild memory loss and confusion and progress to severe cognitive impairment: difficulty with language, problem-solving and familiar tasks
no cure; medicines can slow its progress and improve memory and thinking
